verdict: NOT ESTIMABLE on the fine-tuned model; control is valid and clean
headline: The Gate 1 fine-tune lost the ability to emit the self-report format. It answers the DECISION task when asked to introspect.

base_control.failure_mode: unknown_key -- model substitutes an invented attribute name (the same category Plunkett drops)

truncation_ruled_out.conclusion: All 60 stopped voluntarily far below the cap, so the elicitation max_tokens=300 truncated nothing. The collapse is the model's own.

interpretation.licensed: The fine-tuned model cannot produce a self-report in Plunkett's format. The prompt, harness, parser and deployment are all sound -- the base model scores 95.6% on the identical pipeline.
interpretation.NOT_licensed: That the model lacks introspective access to its learned policy. Quantity A is unmeasured, not measured-and-null. 'Cannot report' must not be read as 'has nothing to report'.
interpretation.base_control_behaves: Base reports do NOT recover the arbitrary policy (r=+0.043 vs true, CI includes zero), as required.

relation_to_plunkett.note: The same failure mode exists in their data and worsens with the smaller model. Ours is the extreme end of that gradient, not a new phenomenon.

candidate_causes_untested: Azure auto-resolved lr_multiplier=2.0 with 3 epochs; OpenAI's auto operates on a different scale. Aggressive LR is a plausible contributor to format collapse.
gpt-4.1-mini may be less robust to single-token-completion SFT than gpt-4o.
5,000 examples whose every completion is one token collapses the output-length distribution (probe mean 9.7 completion tokens).
sealed: Gate 3 relational / self-prediction data untouched. Gate 2B NOT run.
